drafts.title: 70% range at 20 degrees. Warm the car on the wall, not the battery
drafts.angle: First real cold mornings on the Western Slope. The one habit that saves winter range is preheating while plugged in, so the heat comes from the garage outlet instead of the pack. Not a repeat of the Fri AAA $32/$77 cost draft and not his I-70 commute post.
drafts.body: 70%. That's about how much range an EV keeps at 20 degrees. My fix costs [___ cents] a morning: the car warms up on the wall plug at [___ AM], not the battery. Do you schedule yours or start it from the app?
drafts.framework_body:
70%. That's about how much range an EV keeps when it's 20 degrees out.

First real cold mornings here on the Western Slope, so here's the one habit I'd tell any new owner. Warm the car while it's still plugged in. The heat comes off the wall outlet, not the battery. My car is scheduled for [___ AM] and it costs me about [___ cents] a morning.

A few other things that help: heated seat on, cabin a couple degrees cooler, and check your tires after a cold snap because they lose about a pound for every 10 degrees.

The range comes back when it warms up. It's not damage, it's just physics.

[photo: app showing the schedule / frosty driveway]

Do you schedule yours or start it from the app?
bullets: Recurrent US data (via ev.guru, 2026): EVs keep about 78% of their best range at 32F and about 70% at 20F. The loss is temporary and comes back when it warms up.
Tesla's Model Y owner's manual says to start climate about 30 to 45 minutes before you leave, and Scheduled Precondition can have cabin and battery warm at your departure time.
Preheating while plugged in pulls that energy from the grid instead of the battery (fueleconomy.gov, AAA, and Recurrent all say so).
Heated seats and wheel use less energy than blasting cabin heat. Tire pressure drops about 1 PSI for every 10F drop.
drafts.pixel: 15 seconds in the cold garage: phone shows the schedule, open the door to a warm cabin. "It's 20-something out. Car's already warm. Didn't touch the battery."
drafts.premium_target: A verified cold-climate Tesla owner posting a winter range screenshot. Reply with your own preheat number.

drafts.framework_body:
$5.16 more a month. That's the average Xcel gas bump that kicked in Oct 6.

It could have been worse. Xcel asked for about $7.59 and the PUC cut it down. Still, my first real heating bill of the season came in at [$___].

Here's the part that gets me. Same month, my car's fuel came out of the garage outlet for about [$___]. One bill I can't do much about yet. The other one I already fixed.

If money's tight, ask Xcel about the Gas Affordability Program. There's an extra $5 million in it this time. And if your furnace is getting old, this is the winter to at least price out a heat pump.

[photo: Xcel bill with account number blurred]

Revenue increase cut from $190M requested to $122.7M approved.
$5M shareholder-funded add to Xcel's Gas Affordability Program for income-qualified customers.

drafts.title: Colorado EV share got cut in half. Here's why I'm still plugged in
drafts.angle: His neighbors are going hybrid. He gives honest owner math without knocking anyone. Not used-price tracking, not lease deals.
drafts.body: 10.2%. That's Colorado's EV share of new cars this year, down from 21.8%. Lots of neighbors went hybrid. I get it. But my fuel is [$___ a month] from the garage. What would make you pick plug over pump?
drafts.framework_body:
10.2%. That's Colorado's EV share of new cars this year. Last year it was 21.8%.

Hybrids jumped from 13% to 19%. A lot of my neighbors went that way, and honestly I get it. The federal credit went away, rates are high, and the sticker on most EVs still runs higher.

No knock on hybrids. They're a real step up from a gas-only car.

But for somebody who already has the car and a plug in the garage, the monthly number still wins. Mine runs about [$___ a month] to fuel. No gas station on the way home.

[photo: Model Y in the driveway]

What would make you pick plug over pump?
bullets: Colorado Sun (Nov 4, 2026), Colorado Auto Dealers Association data: EV share of new sales fell from 21.8% (first 9 months of 2025) to 10.2% (2026).
Hybrids rose from 13.1% to 19% of new sales.
Tesla Colorado sales went from 8,290 to 6,088, down about 27%, still the top EV brand.
Overall Colorado new car sales down 14.7%, blamed on lost federal EV aid, high rates, and EV price premiums; gas up since spring.
drafts.pixel: Standing by the Model Y with a gas station in the background: "Colorado's buying hybrids. Here's my monthly number."
drafts.premium_target: A verified Colorado or Denver reporter or EV account sharing the CADA numbers. One-line owner take.

drafts.title: AI shopping bots failed 43% of tests. You press Buy
drafts.angle: Holiday shopping season. Use AI to research and compare, then you press Buy yourself. Practical and calm, fits AI less scary without hype or fear.
drafts.body: 43%. That's how often AI shopping bots failed Visa's buying test. Half the misses still bought the wrong thing. I use AI to [compare ___], then I press Buy myself. Would you let a bot spend your money yet?
drafts.framework_body:
43%. That's how often AI shopping bots failed Visa's new buying test.

They ran 22 different AI models through 15 real shopping jobs like a TV or a laptop. More than half the misses still bought something that didn't fit. The best one got it right about 82% of the time. The worst, about 29%.

Here's how I use it. I let AI [compare ___ / find me three options], then I look and I press Buy myself.

Tip for parents and grandparents: tell it your budget and your must-haves right up front. The bots that asked more questions did a lot better.

AI is a great shopping helper. It's not ready to hold your wallet.

Would you let a bot spend your money yet?
bullets: Visa press release (Nov 5, 2026): 22 AI models from 12 labs, 15 shopping tasks (TV, laptop, personal care appliance).
Passed 57.2% of runs and failed 42.8%. Best model 82.2%, worst 28.9%.
In 54% of failed runs the AI still bought something that didn't fit the ask.
Models that asked more questions did better: 70.2% vs 44.4%.
drafts.pixel: Phone in hand: "I let AI pick three TVs. I bought the one I wanted. That's the deal."
drafts.premium_target: A verified tech or personal-finance account sharing the Visa benchmark. One-line "helper, not wallet" reply.
